page: Microsoft Azure L8as_v4 is a virtual machine instance from the Lasv4 family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features an AMD EPYC 9V74 processor based on the x86_64 architecture, configured with 8 dedicated vCPUs across 4 physical cores with multithreading enabled. The CPU operates at a clock speed of 3.7 GHz and includes 32 MB of L3 cache. The instance is equipped with 64.0 GB of system memory, providing a high memory-to-core ratio of 8.0 GB per vCPU. It includes 1920 GB of local storage and is Premium Storage capable, though it does not bundle any complimentary public IPv4 addresses or GPU hardware.

Performance benchmarks indicate strong single-core capabilities, with stress-ng single-core CPU and Geekbench single-core scores placing in the top 25%. This strong single-core performance is also reflected in text processing tasks. However, multi-core performance and memory write bandwidth fall into the average tier. A notable hardware tradeoff is observed in the memory subsystem: while cached small-block read-only memory bandwidth is average at 607.39 GB/sec, the uncached large-block read-only memory bandwidth is weak, measuring at 38.85 GB/sec, which places it in the bottom 25% of tested servers.

Given the 1920 GB of local storage and high memory allocation, the L8as_v4 is well-suited for storage-intensive and database workloads, such as relational databases, caching layers, and medium-scale data processing. From a cost-efficiency perspective, the instance offers a dense combination of local storage and memory relative to its 8 vCPU compute profile, making it a viable option for workloads that require substantial local disk space and memory capacity without needing massive multi-core compute scaling.
